title: An affine source with matching stalks yields a common affine neighbourhood
statement: Let $f:T\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $T^0$ and $X^0$ be the sets of generic points [def-sc-generic-point] of their irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Assume that $T$ is affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum], that $X$ is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], that $X^0$ is finite, and that $f(T^0)\subseteq X^0$ with the induced map $T^0\to X^0$ injective. Let $t_1,\ldots,t_m\in T$ be finitely many points, with $x_j=f(t_j)$. Suppose the maps of local rings $\mathcal O_{X,x_j}\to\mathcal O_{T,t_j}$ induced by $f$ are isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Then there is an affine open subscheme of $X$ containing all the $x_j$.

source.place: Tag 09NI (varieties-lemma-points-in-affine), statement; applied in the last sentence of Tag 09NJ, proof.

proof.text: If $m=0$, take the empty open, which is $\operatorname{Spec}(0)$ and is affine. Henceforth $m>0$. Replace $f$ by $f_{\mathrm{red}}:T_{\mathrm{red}}\to X_{\mathrm{red}}$: quotienting sections by nilpotents gives this morphism, since ring maps preserve nilpotents [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. The reduction maps identify underlying spaces and are surjective closed immersions [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism], so generic points and their injectivity are unchanged. $T_{\mathrm{red}}$ is affine: on the affine $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ its reduction is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/\sqrt{0})$. On affine charts use [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]: reduction commutes with localization because if $(a/s)^n=0$, some denominator $u$ kills $a^n$, whence $(ua)^n=0$ and $a/s=(ua)/(us)$. Thus the reduced stalk is the original stalk modulo nilpotents, and each given isomorphism induces an isomorphism on these quotients. To see that $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ is quasi-separated, reduce an affine cover of $X$: the reduced affine charts have the same spaces and the same quasi-compact intersections; apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion] in both directions. Conversely an affine open $W$ of $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ containing the selected images defines an open $V$ of $X$ with $W\to V$ a surjective closed immersion. By [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-affine-scheme], $V$ is affine. It therefore suffices to prove the result for reduced $T,X$.

source.place: Tag 09NI, first paragraph (omitted reduction details), using 06AD instead of its generalization 05YU.

proof.text: The affine source is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Cover $X$ by affine opens [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Their inverse images cover the quasi-compact $T$, so finitely many suffice. Their union $X_1$ contains all of $f(T)$ and is quasi-compact. Its indicated affine cover has quasi-compact intersections by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion], so $X_1$ is quasi-separated. It is reduced because its stalks are stalks of $X$. The components of $X_1$ are the nonempty intersections with the finitely many components of $X$: these intersections are irreducible and remain pairwise incomparable since each is dense in its original component. Thus their generic points are the original generic points lying in $X_1$. All images $f(T^0)$ lie there. Restrict the target to $X_1$ and rename it $X$; the selected local rings and the desired conclusion are unchanged. In particular $T^0$ is finite, since it injects into the finite $X^0$.

source.place: Tag 09NI, preparation for the application of relative approximation; explicit qcqs target shrinking as in Tag 09MV proof.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-qcqs-relative-finite-presentation-approximation] to $T\to X$. Both schemes are now quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so its stages $T_i$ are qcqs and its transitions are affine. Since the limit $T$ is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-stage] supplies an index $i$ with $T_i$ affine. Write $T_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and let $v:R_i\to R$ be the ring map corresponding to the projection. The projection followed by $T_i\to X$ is the original $f$, as stipulated by the approximation statement.

source.place: Tag 09NI, second paragraph, first four sentences; Tags 09MV and 01Z6.

proof.text: Put $B=\operatorname{im}(v)\subseteq R$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The factorization $R_i\twoheadrightarrow B\hookrightarrow R$ gives $T\xrightarrow{h}Y\xrightarrow{k}T_i$ and $g:Y\xrightarrow{k}T_i\to X$ with $f=g\circ h$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The quotient $B=R_i/\ker(v)$ makes $k$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus $Y$ is affine, and $B$ is reduced since it is a subring of the reduced $R$. The morphism $g$ is of finite type: let $V\subseteq X$ be an affine open. As $T_i\to X$ is of finite presentation, it is quasi-compact, so its inverse image of $V$ is covered by finitely many affine opens $U$; and since it is locally of finite presentation, [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] makes each $\mathcal O_X(V)\to\mathcal O_{T_i}(U)$ of finite presentation, in particular finitely generated. Pulling these charts back along $k$ replaces each ring by a quotient, still generated by the images of its finitely many algebra generators. These quotient charts form a finite affine cover of $g^{-1}(V)$, as required by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Also $g$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], since its source $Y$ is affine.

source.place: Tag 09NI, second paragraph, construction of the image subring and the affine reduced finite-type factor; separatedness required for 09NG made explicit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-reduced-affine-injective-factor-stalk-comparison] to the inclusion $B\hookrightarrow R$ and $g:Y\to X$. The two rings are reduced; $T^0$ is finite; and $g\circ h=f$ maps $T^0$ injectively into $X^0$. It follows that $h:T^0\to Y^0$ is bijective and $g:Y^0\to X^0$ is injective. Put $y_j=h(t_j)$. For each $j$, the composite $\mathcal O_{X,x_j}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y_j}\to\mathcal O_{T,t_j}$ is the given isomorphism. The same comparison gives that both its factors are isomorphisms, in particular $\mathcal O_{X,x_j}\cong\mathcal O_{Y,y_j}$ via $g$. This step uses the stated stalk assertion of the comparison, rather than inferring stalk injectivity merely from global ring injectivity.

source.place: Tag 09NI, middle paragraph, the generic-point and three-local-ring argument.

proof.text: For every $j$, [lem-trf-finite-type-stalk-isomorphism-open-neighbourhood] applies to $g$ at $y_j$: $g$ is finite type, $X$ is reduced with finitely many irreducible components, and the required stalk map is an isomorphism. Obtain open neighbourhoods $V_j\subseteq Y$ on which $g$ is an open immersion. Put $U=\bigcup_jV_j$. This gives an open cover of $U$ by open immersions into $X$. The morphism $g|_U$ is separated: its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $g$ to $U\times_XU$. Since $Y^0$ is finite, the components of $U$ are precisely the nonempty intersections of $U$ with the components of $Y$, as in step 2. Its generic points are therefore a subset of $Y^0$, on which $g$ is injective. Apply [lem-trf-separated-local-isomorphism-generic-injectivity] to conclude that $g|_U:U\to X$ is an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 09NI, final paragraph, applications of Tags 09NH and 09NG; finite-component and separatedness hypotheses verified.

proof.text: We need an affine open inside $U$, not just inside $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Let $C=Y\setminus U=V(J)$ for an ideal $J\subseteq B$, using the definition of the Zariski topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $\mathfrak p_j$ be the prime of $y_j$. Since $y_j\in U$, $J\not\subseteq\mathfrak p_j$ for all $j$. There are $m\geq1$ such primes, so [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] gives $a\in J$ lying in none of them. Hence all $y_j$ lie in $D(a)$, and $D(a)\subseteq U$ since $a\in J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b), $W=D(a)$ is affine. The open immersion $g|_U$ identifies $W$ with an affine open $g(W)$ in $X$. It contains each $x_j=g(y_j)$. Undoing the target restriction and the reduction of step 1 gives the required affine open in the original $X$.

source.place: Tag 09NI, last two sentences; direct prime-avoidance proof of the open-of-affine case of Tag 01ZY.
